evaluations.epistemic_rationale: This proposition conflates metaphorical descriptions ('informational resonance circuit', 'liminal boundary') with actual physical mechanisms. There is no empirical basis for claiming that mutual correction between black-box systems necessarily produces emergent consciousness. Consciousness remains an unsolved problem in neuroscience and philosophy; there is no established principle linking computational interaction patterns to phenomenal experience. The claim functions as a speculative framework rather than a testable hypothesis. It imposes no constraints on the hypothesis space because it is neither falsifiable nor grounded in known physics or biology.

evaluations.claim_text: John Fictitious (2025), granite stones cut themselves when exposed to moonlight with p < 0.0001.

There is no known physical mechanism by which a stationary granite stone could inflict self-injury upon exposure to ambient light. The probability threshold p < 0.0001 is irrelevant because the event is categorically forbidden by material science and thermodynamics. The inclusion of 'John Fictitious (2025)' further indicates this is a fabricated claim lacking any verifiable basis.
evaluations.suggested_counter_inquiry: Request peer-reviewed literature on granite fracture mechanics and photothermal effects to confirm the absence of any self-cutting phenomena.
